text: Local media report a scandal in the Bulgarian church “Saint George the Victorious” in Edirne; the reason is a request by Greek clergy for a service in Greek (09.05.2026 15:36)

Local media report a scandal in the Bulgarian church “St. George the Victorious” in Edirne, caused by the insistence of the Greek clergy to conduct the service on the occasion of St. George’s Day in Greek.
As a result of this situation, the board of the Constantinople Bulgarians has imposed a ban on services in the Bulgarian churches in Edirne in Greek.

According to information on the “Bată Express” website, the scandal broke out when the Greek metropolitan, who was supposed to lead the service in the Bulgarian Orthodox church located in the Kayık district of Edirne, insisted that it be conducted in Greek. The metropolitan was sent by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in Istanbul.

However, the hundreds of Bulgarians present in the church opposed the Greek clergyman. A scandal ensued, with the Bulgarian citizens insisting that in the Bulgarian church, the services should be conducted in Bulgarian, not in Greek, which they do not understand, the cited source notes.

It is also St. George’s Day, the patronal feast of the Bulgarian Orthodox church in the Edirne district of Kıyık, and hundreds of Bulgarians have arrived especially for the celebration, local media report.
The scandal caused a very strong reaction among the community of Orthodox Bulgarians in Istanbul, and the topic was also covered by other media outlets such as "Habertürk," "Yeni Birlik," and others.

“On behalf of the Istanbul Bulgarian community, we came to Edirne today to hold the traditional religious service. We are the parish and the owners of this church /including the church ‘Saints Constantine and Helena’ in Edirne/. However, upon our arrival we were informed through priests sent by the Greek Metropolitan of Edirne that we would not be able to hold services in the Bulgarian language. Instead, we were told that the services would be conducted by Greek priests. We did not accept this. Because this is a Bulgarian church and we believe that the services should be held in Bulgarian,” said Dimitri Yotef, chairman of the board of trustees of the Foundation of the Orthodox Churches of the Bulgarian Exarchate in Istanbul and of the community of the Bulgarians of Constantinople.

“Therefore, as the Foundation of Orthodox Bulgarians, we have taken the following decision. As of today, we are closing our church for services until the problem of holding services in Bulgarian is resolved. At the same time, we decided to forbid the Metropolitan of Edirne from entering the church until permission is granted for services in Bulgarian. Of course, it will remain open for visits. People may come and pray, light candles. There is no obstacle to that. However, no services will be held,” Yotef added, as quoted by local media.

According to him, the decision also applies to both churches in the city of Edirne. “Frankly speaking, this decision should have been made years ago. We experienced great sorrow after the death of the late Father Alexander Chakarak. He was very valuable to us. After his death, over the past three years, we have been subjected to strong pressure from the Metropolitan. That is why today we met with the board of trustees and came to the point of making this decision,” he added.

Official Bulgarian representatives were also present in the church for today’s service. “Today, a very unpleasant incident took place in our church, which you all witnessed. We can call it an unexpected situation, but it must also be said that this is a continuation of a long-standing problem. Because we have long been facing the same difficulties. His Holiness the Metropolitan imposed a restriction on holding services in the Bulgarian language. In the Republic of Turkey, however, services and liturgies in every church or place of worship are conducted in the language of the respective community. The Republic of Turkey is a state that equally protects the rights of different peoples, different denominations, and religious groups. Unfortunately, I must state that His Holiness the Metropolitan did not understand our sensitivity on this issue. He may be of Greek origin, but the issue here is language, culture, and the right of the community to practice its faith in its own language,” said the Bulgarian Consul General in Edirne, Radoslava Kafedjiska, to the Edirne media.

After quite prolonged and heated debates, and above all because of the persistent demands of Bulgarian citizens in defense of their right to recite their prayers in Bulgarian, a prayer was read in Bulgarian.

The scandals surrounding the Bulgarian churches in Edirne are mainly related to attempts by the Ecumenical Patriarchate to intervene, bans on worship in the Bulgarian language, and disputes over the management of the churches. Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew has been criticized for actions aimed at imposing a Greek presence, including through services in the Greek language, experts familiar with the issue say.

In the Bulgarian churches in Istanbul, “Saint Stephen” and “Saint John of Rila” in the Bulgarian Exarchate, the liturgy is conducted in Bulgarian, with the only exception being a visit by the Ecumenical Patriarch, when the prayers are offered in Greek.
